key_insight: An LLM-guided evolutionary search can discover interpretable fermion-to-qubit encodings with verified higher code distance and better qubit compression than prior Generalized Superfast Encoding constructions.
engineering_relevance: For molecular quantum simulation, these encodings reduce data-qubit overhead while preserving strict stabilizer-coset correctness, making them attractive as resource-efficient front ends for future algorithms.
method: LLM edits constructor programs in an evolutionary loop
An external verifier scores exact code distance and compression
High-scoring programs are retained and re-mutated to refine encoding rules
evidence_signal: On tested molecular instances, the search produced exact distance-5 codes and a distance-6 code on one 20-mode case, while using 4.2–5.0× fewer data qubits and showing 3.4–8.2× lower logical-failure rates in a memory comparison.
watch_item: The reported gains are limited to verified encoding and memory-resource metrics; the authors do not claim circuit-level fault-tolerance or Trotter-cost improvements.
paper_title: Evolving Quantum Error-Correcting Encodings for Molecular Simulation
